entry.title: P1 deps: ts-fsrs for the scheduler, a bundle-safe ed25519 verifier, a…
entry.content:
P1 deps: ts-fsrs for the scheduler, a bundle-safe ed25519 verifier, and tools/soundbank

The one P1 task allowed to touch a manifest, so every dependency P1 needs lands here
and no later task has to edit a lockfile.

packages/core: ts-fsrs@5.4.2 (MIT, zero runtime dependencies, `engines.node >=20`). The
plan names FSRS for `scheduler/`; a hand-rolled copy of a published algorithm is the kind
of thing whose bugs only show up as a learner's retention curve months later, so it is a
real dependency, not vendored. It is pure TS, so `packages/core`'s purity gate is
untouched.

packages/schema: @noble/ed25519@3.2.0 + @noble/hashes@2.4.0 (both MIT, zero runtime
dependencies). `packages/schema/keys/pack-signing.pub` has to be verified *on device*,
where there is no `node:crypto` and, on React Native, no WebCrypto `subtle` either — so
the async default hash path is not available and the sync sha512 hook is the shipping
one. In @noble/ed25519 v3 that hook is `ed.hashes.sha512`, not v2's `ed.etc.sha512Sync`:

    import { sha512 } from '@noble/hashes/sha2.js';
    ed.hashes.sha512 = (...m) => sha512(ed.etc.concatBytes(...m));

P0's hand-rolled SPKI parser stays exactly as it is; the verifier is the second half, and
the schema task holds it against `node:crypto` in a test. Measured here before choosing
it (node v24.18.0, this lockfile): noble verifies a `node:crypto` ed25519 signature,
rejects a one-bit-tampered message, and `node:crypto` verifies a noble signature over a
key it agrees is ed25519.

Nothing was added to apps/mobile. P1 is an engine phase and needed no Expo package, so
`npx expo install` was not run and the Reanimated/worklets pin is untouched
(INV-PLAT-01). `patches/expo-modules-jsi@57.1.0.patch` and its `patchedDependencies`
entry are untouched.

tools/soundbank: a second uv project for the P1 sound-synthesis script — numpy 2.5.3 +
soundfile 0.14.0, pinned to Python 3.12 like coursekit. It is separate from
`tools/coursekit` so that `pack-ci.yml`'s `coursekit validate` never resolves numpy and a
sound bake never resolves a morphology stack. **No Python audio codec**: encoding is the
system ffmpeg (`/opt/homebrew/bin/ffmpeg`, with libopus; `opusenc` is not installed).
Proved end to end before committing — numpy array -> `soundfile` WAV (24,044 B) ->
`ffmpeg -c:a libopus -b:a 20k` -> 753 B, `ffprobe` reporting `codec_name=opus`,
`sample_rate=48000`. `tools/coursekit/uv.lock` did not change; `uv sync` on it is green.

Root scripts: `test:golden-migrations` added for the P1 migration corpus.
`test:falsify`, `test:coverage-map` and `invariants:check` all still resolve and run.

Verified: `pnpm install` then `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` a no-op (179 ms, "Already
up to date"); `pnpm lint`, `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm test` 61/61 in 12 files;
`invariants:check` in sync at 424 ids; `coverage-map` 6/6 owned ids with a test,
INV-PLAT-01 among them; `uv sync` green for both uv projects.

P0: patch expo-modules-jsi for Xcode 26.2 and run the Android maestro command on one line

expo-modules-jsi@57.1.0 annotates two RuntimeScheduler constructors with
SWIFT_RETURNS_RETAINED, which Swift 6.2.3+ (Xcode 26.2+) rejects; the annotation

#50061, #50062; the fix PR #49740 was closed unmerged). Applied as a pnpm patch so
every install, local and CI, gets the same two-line change.

reactivecircus/android-emulator-runner executes each script line as its own sh -c,

(CI round 3: 'Flow path does not exist: .../\'). One line now.

entry.title: P0 CI round 3: expo-modules-jsi fails at BOTH ends of the Xcode range
entry.content:
P0 CI round 3: expo-modules-jsi fails at BOTH ends of the Xcode range

Round 2's pin was half right and the wrong half was the measurable one. Both ends
now measured rather than reasoned about:

  * Xcode 26.2 (Swift 6.2.3) fails LOUDLY — RuntimeScheduler.h:53 and :61,
    SWIFT_RETURNS_RETAINED on a type that is not a SWIFT_SHARED_REFERENCE, exit 65.
    Reproduced locally and reduced to a 15-line repro with no Expo, no React Native.
  * Xcode 16.4 (Swift 6.1, the image default, what round 2 pinned) fails QUIETLY at the
    SAME phase. Run 34634498819: `[CP-User] Build ExpoModulesJSI xcframework` starts at
    18:45:31, the next line is 18:45:47, and the build then prints `0 error(s), and 1
    warning(s)` and exits 65. A script phase's stdout does not reach Expo's pretty
    printer, so a build that failed reports no errors at all. 16.4 is too old to build a
    framework SDK 57 compiles from source at pod time.

The pin moves inside the range to 26.1.1 — the newest Xcode predating the 26.2 check,
and the line Expo SDK 57 shipped against. iPhone 17 @ iOS-26-1 comes back with it.

Also added `Why the build failed`, an `if: failure()` step that re-runs xcodebuild raw
and tails 200 lines. The incremental build fails again in seconds at the same phase,
this time with the phase's own output. Round 2 cost a full CI round to learn one bit —
"16.4 also fails" — because nothing printed why. That does not happen twice.

Everything else from round 2 stands and is unrelated to the pin: the vitest per-project
timeout, and `set -eu` for dash in the emulator action.

entry.title: P0 CI round 2: the 5s vitest default and dash in the emulator action
entry.content:
P0 CI round 2: the 5s vitest default and dash in the emulator action

Both failures are from the first real run of these jobs (34634498780, 34634498819).
Neither is visible locally, and neither says what it is.

1. ci.yml RED: `Error: Test timed out in 5000ms` at streak.test.ts:68 and :173 — the
   two four-zone properties, 40,000 cases each. They take ~3.5 s on this Mac and the
   whole suite runs about 2.5x slower on ubuntu-latest, so 5,000 ms is the wrong side
   of the line there and the right side here. 5,000 ms is vitest's default, not a
   decision anybody made about this suite; the P0 gate is the case count. So the
   timeout is now named in vitest.config.ts at 60 s — about seven times the slowest
   measured case, still short enough that a real hang is a failure rather than the
   job's 90 minutes.

   The obvious repair for a slow property is to cut the runs, which is exactly what
   PROPERTY_RUNS exists to prevent, so property-gates.test.ts now holds the timeout
   too — and holds it PER PROJECT. A `testTimeout` at the top level of vitest.config.ts
   is silently ignored by inline `projects`: probed with a test that sleeps 6 s, which
   still failed at 5000ms. That mutant is killed by the new test; without it, this
   "fix" would have been a no-op that looked exactly like a fix and cost another round.

2. Android emulator RED: `sh: 1: set: Illegal option -o pipefail`, exit 2.
   reactivecircus/android-emulator-runner runs `script:` with /usr/bin/sh — dash on
   ubuntu-latest — so the block died on its first line, before adb. The job then
   failed on a missing JUnit report, which reads as an emulator or a Maestro problem
   and is neither. `set -eu` there (the script has no pipes); every other `run:` in the
   workflow is bash and keeps pipefail.

The gate file grew past its name and is now native-e2e-gates.test.ts: it holds the
screenshot contract, the Xcode pin and the emulator shell — all three found by running
the workflow, all three failing in a way that points somewhere else.

Green in this run and kept: INV-PLAT-02 prebuild determinism, and `flows exist`.

entry.title: P0: make the screenshot contract match what Maestro does, and pin the…
entry.content:
P0: make the screenshot contract match what Maestro does, and pin the iOS toolchain

Three defects found by running the thing rather than reading it. All of them were
invisible from a passing flow, which is the point.

1. THE SCREENSHOT CONTRACT DID NOT WORK. Measured on Maestro 2.10.0 against
   emulator-5554, 2026-09-11:
     * `takeScreenshot` is always resolved inside Maestro's OWN run directory, as
       <run-dir>/<flow>/takeScreenshot/<the given path>.png. It is never relative to
       the working directory, so no flow can write into e2e/artifacts/ however the
       path is spelled.
     * a flow-level `env:` default WINS over `maestro test -e NAME=...`. The flow
       defaulted ARTIFACT_DIR, so CI's value was discarded and every run on every sha
       wrote the same literal e2e/artifacts/local/p0-db-path.png — inside the run
       directory. Probed with -e ARTIFACT_DIR=ZZZ_OVERRIDE_MARKER: the marker never
       appeared.
   The jobs only avoided going red because --debug-output happened to nest the run
   directory under ARTIFACT_DIR, so `find -name '*.png'` found a frame at a path that
   named neither the sha nor the platform. Delete that one flag and the check fails on
   a passing flow.
   Now: the flow names its frame and nothing else, the jobs aim the run directory with
   --test-output-dir, and a step copies each PNG up to $ARTIFACT_DIR/screenshots/
   <flow>-<name>.png — flat, no timestamp — and fails the job if it collected none.
   NOT --flatten-debug-output: on 2.10.0 that makes the run write into $HOME and never
   create --test-output-dir at all (measured).

2. THE iOS JOB WOULD HAVE BUILT ON A TOOLCHAIN THAT CANNOT BUILD THIS APP. Reproduced
   here: under Xcode 26.2 (17C52, Apple Swift 6.2.3) the ExpoModulesJSI xcframework
   phase fails with 2 errors, xcodebuild exit 65 —
     RuntimeScheduler.h:53:26: 'RuntimeScheduler' cannot be annotated with either
     SWIFT_RETURNS_RETAINED or SWIFT_RETURNS_UNRETAINED because it is not returning a
     SWIFT_SHARED_REFERENCE type
   and again at :61. expo-modules-jsi@57.1.0's own header against a tightened C++
   interop check in Swift 6.2; the package builds that framework from source at pod
   time, so there is no prebuilt slice to fall back to. The macos-15 image carries
   Xcode 16.4 through 26.3 and the job took whatever was default, so this was one image
   bump away from red for a reason no log would explain. XCODE_APP now pins 16.4
   (Swift 6.1, the image default), the job fails loudly if that Xcode is absent rather
   than drifting, SIMULATOR_OS moves to an 18.x runtime because 16.4 carries no iOS 26
   one, and runner.txt records the Xcode that actually ran. The fix belongs upstream in
   expo/expo; raise the pin when it lands, not hopefully.

3. THE INVARIANT COVERAGE SCAN WALKED THE GENERATED NATIVE TREES. Its pattern matches
   any .yaml, because Maestro flows are yaml and carry invariant ids — and
   `expo prebuild` fills apps/mobile/ios with vendored ones. A prebuilt checkout
   reported 27 test files instead of 12, fifteen of them CocoaPods dSYM relocation
   maps. Nothing in a generated, gitignored tree may decide whether an invariant has an
   owning test. Skipped by PATH, not by the names ios/android, so a future
   packages/core/src/platform/ios test does not vanish in silence — verified both ways.

packages/testkit/src/screenshot-contract.test.ts holds (1) and (2). It reads the
workflow with whole-line comments stripped, because the comments quote the superseded
spellings to warn people off them and the first draft of the gate flagged its own
warning as a usage. Both mutants killed: restoring ${ARTIFACT_DIR} in the flow and
-e ARTIFACT_DIR= in the workflow turns it red on two tests.

Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01GjKXj51yvLrSnxgMyWyTod

entry.title: P0: the diagnostics surface must exist in the Release build the gate …
entry.content:
P0: the diagnostics surface must exist in the Release build the gate runs against

native-e2e builds Release on both platforms on purpose — Release embeds the JS
bundle, which is what makes `--no-bundler` honest. `__DEV__` is false there, and
DevDiagnostics was gated on `__DEV__`, so the INV-PER-06 flow long-pressed the
title and got nothing: `Assertion is false: id: dev-diagnostics is visible`
(measured on emulator-5554, 32s). Two branches each did the right thing alone and
the pair did not work.

The gate is now `__DEV__ OR EXPO_PUBLIC_FREELINGO_E2E=1`. Metro inlines
EXPO_PUBLIC_* at bundle time, so a store build that does not set it does not merely
hide the screen — it does not contain the branch that opens it. The reference has
to stay a literal `process.env.EXPO_PUBLIC_FREELINGO_E2E` member access, because a
computed lookup is not substituted and would yield undefined in a release bundle
with no error.

The flag is set workflow-level in native-e2e.yml, not per-step: the Android build
and flow run inside a third-party action's `script:`, which never sees a step-level
env of ours.

packages/testkit/src/diagnostics-gate.test.ts holds the three halves together — the
rule, App.tsx's use of it, and the workflow setting it for both builds — because
nothing else does. Remove one and the device gate goes quiet rather than red.

entry.content:
P0: pack signing key custody, the ARTIFACT_DIR screenshot contract, and two stale READMEs

The two P0 branches are merged. Three things they each left to the integration,
because each sat in the other's file lane:

- Signing key. ed25519 generated at P0; the private half went straight into the
  PACK_SIGNING_KEY Actions secret and was removed with rm -P, never printed. The public
  half is committed and ships in the app. packages/schema/src/signing.ts is custody only
  — the path, the secret name, and a parser that refuses anything that is not an ed25519
  SPKI, hand-rolled because the app has no node:crypto and a parser that works only on
  the test runner proves nothing about what ships. The test holds it against node:crypto
  and checks it rejects a P-256 key, prose, an empty block and a truncation. It does NOT
  claim INV-PACK-18: verify-before-install lands at P2 with the installer.

- The screenshot contract. native-e2e fails a job if no .png reaches ${ARTIFACT_DIR},
  and p0-db-path.yaml took no screenshot, so both device jobs would have gone red on a
  passing flow. The flow now shoots last — after every assertion, so the frame is of a
  screen that was checked — and carries a local default in its env: block so it still
  runs from a checkout without arguments.

- e2e/README.md still said 'P0 status: no flows yet' and that the maestro step is
  commented out until P3. False in every clause since the flow landed.

entry.title: p0/persistence: make the device gate name the cache region, not just …
entry.content:
p0/persistence: make the device gate name the cache region, not just the directory

`.*/packs/?` passed for any path ending in `packs`, so the assertion would have stayed
green if the packs directory ever moved next to the progress DB in the document region —
which is precisely the regression INV-PACK-11 exists to catch. The assertion now names the
region on each platform (`/Library/Caches` on iOS, `/cache` on Android) in the same
single-alternation style as the `db-path` row above it, so the two device gates cannot
drift apart.

Also asserts `pre-migration-backup` is `none`. The flow launches with `clearState: true`,
so the DB is created straight at the latest `user_version` and there is no earlier file to
protect; a copy at that point would mean the pre-migration path fired on a database that
never had a previous schema.

Verified on the Pixel_3a_API_34 emulator (Android 14, arm64, emulator-5554): flow passed
in 18s, 1/1. db-path file:///data/user/0/org.freelingo.app/files/freelingo-progress.db
with -wal and -shm beside it, journal_mode wal, user_version 1, packs-dir
file:///data/user/0/org.freelingo.app/cache/packs/ (created, empty), packs-excluded true,
pre-migration-backup none. `npx expo prebuild --clean` regenerated both native trees and
the config plugin wrote res/xml/backup_rules.xml and res/xml/data_extraction_rules.xml with
android:fullBackupContent and android:dataExtractionRules on <application>.

iOS is STILL not verified, for the same upstream reason and now with a 15-line repro that
takes Expo and React Native out of the picture: under the only Xcode on this machine
(26.2, Swift 6.2.3) a C++ class carrying a trailing SWIFT_SHARED_REFERENCE attribute cannot
annotate its constructors SWIFT_RETURNS_RETAINED — the importer rejects them with "not
returning a SWIFT_SHARED_REFERENCE type". expo-modules-jsi@57.1.0 does exactly that in
apple/Sources/ExpoModulesJSI-Cxx/include/RuntimeScheduler.h:53 and :61, and its xcframework
is built from source at pod build time (the shipped slices are 20K stubs), so there is no
prebuilt binary to fall back to. 57.1.0 is the newest release in the SDK 57 line. The fix
belongs upstream; patching a dependency's header to turn the gate green would be the kind
of lie this repo's gates exist to prevent.

entry.title: p0/persistence: open the progress DB on device and prove the path (IN…
entry.content:
p0/persistence: open the progress DB on device and prove the path (INV-PER-06)

The persistence layout stops being a table of constants and becomes something the
app actually does, checked on a device rather than asserted in a unit test.

packages/core/src/db/
  `Db` (run/all/get/withExclusiveTransaction/close) — the interface both runtimes
  implement. `@freelingo/schema` declares the identical one because it cannot import
  core without a cycle; `apps/mobile/src/db/ExpoDb.ts` types its adapter as core's and
  hands it to schema's `migrate()`, so `pnpm typecheck` catches any drift.

  `persistence.ts` holds the decisions the app shell would otherwise make inline: the
  per-platform persistent-path marker behind `dbPathIsPersistent`, the pre-migration
  copy name `freelingo-pre-v<N>-<ISO8601>.db` (ISO 8601 *basic*, so no colon ever
  enters a filename), and the pruner that keeps the two most recent copies and can
  never name a file it did not create. Five new [INV-PER-06] tests, two of them
  properties at 10,000 cases.

apps/mobile/src/db/
  `ExpoDb` opens the DB in `Paths.document`, sets `PRAGMA journal_mode = WAL` outside
  any transaction, checkpoints and copies the file when a migration is pending, then
  runs the schema registry against `PRAGMA user_version` inside ONE
  `withExclusiveTransactionAsync`. The adapter's `withExclusiveTransaction` joins an
  open transaction rather than nesting, because SQLite has no nested transactions and
  the outermost scope is the one that must commit (INV-CER-01).

  `startPersistence` also creates `Paths.cache/packs` and asks the platform to keep it
  out of device backup, returning every value it learned instead of logging it.

apps/mobile/modules/backup-exclusion/
  A local Expo module: iOS sets `URLResourceValues.isExcludedFromBackup` and returns
  the flag it reads *back* off the file system, so a silent no-op cannot report
  success; Android returns true because exclusion can only be declared, and declares
  it — `app.plugin.js` writes res/xml/backup_rules.xml and data_extraction_rules.xml
  excluding `cache/packs` and sets android:fullBackupContent and
  android:dataExtractionRules on <application> (INV-PACK-11).

DevDiagnostics + e2e/flows/p0-db-path.yaml
  A dev-build-only screen behind a long press on the title, every row carrying a
  testID, and the Maestro flow that reads them on the device.

Two traps found only by building, both fixed in metro.config.js:
  - `disableHierarchicalLookup` is for a hoisted monorepo. Under pnpm it breaks at the
    first transitive import ("Unable to resolve expo-modules-core from expo/src/Expo.ts").
  - Metro does not understand the NodeNext `./db.js` specifiers the workspace packages
    use; they are rewritten, and only for files under packages/.

And one in apps/mobile/.gitignore: the root ignores every directory named ios/ or
android/ at any depth (INV-PLAT-02), which silently swallowed the local module's own
native sources. They are source, not a prebuild output, and are re-included by name.

Verified on a Pixel_3a_API_34 emulator (Android 14, arm64): db at
/data/user/0/org.freelingo.app/files/freelingo-progress.db with -wal and -shm beside
it, journal_mode wal, user_version 1, cache/packs created, packs-excluded true, and
the whole Maestro flow green. The copy-and-prune path was exercised by temporarily
adding migrations v2..v4: three copies taken, oldest deleted, exactly two left.

iOS is NOT verified: expo-modules-jsi@57.1.0 fails to build under the only Xcode on
this machine (26.2 / Swift 6.2.3) — see the report.

entry.content:
ci: do not turn one native-e2e failure into three errors

`if: always()` also fires on cancellation, and the post-run checks wrote into an
artefact directory that does not exist when the job dies before creating it — so a
single early failure produced a missing-report error, a missing-runner.txt error and an
if-no-files-found upload error on top of the real one. The checks now run on
`!cancelled()` and create the directory before writing to it.

Dropped `force-avd-creation: false`: there is no AVD cache yet, so it changes nothing
and implies one exists.

entry.title: ci: real Maestro e2e on simulator and emulator, and a prebuild-drift …
entry.content:
ci: real Maestro e2e on simulator and emulator, and a prebuild-drift gate

native-e2e.yml stops being a placeholder.

flows-present (ubuntu, 10 s) counts the flows first and both device jobs `needs:` it.
`maestro test` over an empty directory exits 0, which is the most expensive way this
workflow could lie: two device builds, twenty minutes each, a green tick and nothing
tested. A flow is a yaml with an `appId:` header, so e2e/flows/README.md is not counted
as one. Exercised in all four states (missing dir, empty dir, prose-only yaml, real
flow) before committing. It is RED until the persistence branch lands
e2e/flows/p0-db-path.yaml, and that is the correct colour for "there are no flows".

ios-simulator (macos-15) and android-emulator (ubuntu + android-emulator-runner, API 34
x86_64): temurin 21 for Maestro's Java 17+ requirement, the curl installer on PATH,
frozen-lockfile install, `expo prebuild --clean`, then `expo run:{ios,android}` in
RELEASE — Release embeds the JS bundle, which is what makes `--no-bundler` honest;
a Debug build with no Metro would launch to a red screen and fail every flow for the
wrong reason. Flows screenshot into `${ARTIFACT_DIR}` (passed with `-e`, so no flow
hard-codes a sha or platform); a step then fails the job if the JUnit report is missing
or no png arrived. Artefacts are e2e-<sha>-ios / -android: upload-artifact@v4 refuses a
duplicate name, so one shared e2e-<sha> would have dropped a platform.

prebuild-determinism is INV-PLAT-02 as a job: nothing tracked under apps/mobile/{ios,
android}, and two prebuilds of the same commit produce the same tree.

Byte-for-byte would have been red on every run. Measured locally, twice: the two trees
agree on 70 files and differ in exactly one 24-hex Xcode object id, minted afresh by
expo-dev-client's plugin for its "Strip Local Network Keys" build phase. Ids are
arbitrary internal names, so the trees are compared up to a consistent renaming of them
(scripts/canonicalise-pbxproj.py). Verified that canonicalisation still catches a changed
build setting and a reordered build phase, and its --self-test asserts that in CI. The
tree hash also covers entry types and symlink targets, so a rename, a dropped symlink and
a new empty directory are drift as well. Ran the job's step verbatim on this machine:
both hashes 8dcab253…, working tree clean afterwards.

Verified against the installed SDK 57 CLI rather than from memory: run:ios takes
--configuration/-d, run:android takes --variant, both take --no-bundler, and prebuild now
documents --no-clean (recreating is the default) while still accepting --clean.

actionlint 1.7.12 + shellcheck clean on all five workflows.

docs/ci.md records what each workflow proves and why the two comparisons are shaped the
way they are; invariants-owned.json keeps its six ids and gains a phaseNote saying which
sections P1 adds.

entry.title: test: every invariant property runs 10,000 cases, in every zone
entry.content:
test: every invariant property runs 10,000 cases, in every zone

Finishes the stopped agent's partial change (cherry-picked as-is, then corrected).

Kept: PROPERTY_RUNS as named config, the independent `referenceStreak`, the committed
DST falsifier inputs, arbInstant.

Corrected three things:

- PROPERTY_RUNS_PER_ZONE was 2_500, i.e. the four-zone properties bought their wall-clock
  by running a quarter of the cases in each zone. The P0 gate is "10,000 cases in four
  zones", so it is now PROPERTY_RUNS *per zone*.

- The four-zone streak property drew 40 dates out of a four-year span. Measured over
  2,500 cases, 2,429 of them had no day anywhere near today: 97% of the budget asserted
  that zero equals zero. Days are now generated as civil-date OFFSETS from today, from
  three shapes (a structural run + gap + older block, a dense coin-flip window, and the
  old sparse shape at low weight). Measured over 20,000 samples: 65.9% anchored, 35.0%
  with a run of 3+, 20.5% with a run of 10+, longest 31. That is what "tight generators,
  not fewer runs" means, and it is cheaper per case as well.

- Dropped a redundant `as LocalDay` cast.

Added two meta-gates, because both failures above were invisible to a green suite:
property-gates.test.ts fails if any numRuns in the tree is below PROPERTY_RUNS, and
arbitraries.test.ts holds the generator's shape floors (a property over a generator that
cannot produce the interesting case is 10,000 cases of nothing).

Killed two hand-written mutants of streakFromDays (non-contiguous count; two-days-ago
anchors) with both DAY-01 tests; pnpm test 7.60s.

entry.content:
core: give INV-CER-01 an engine-side test

The first nightly mutation run scored ceremony/commit.ts at 0.00 with every
mutant marked "no coverage". The only INV-CER-01 tests lived in the schema
project — they exercise the exclusive transaction and call planCommit through
it — but Stryker runs the core project alone, so the pure engine function was
formally unexercised while test:coverage-map read green for the id.

A gate that green-lights untested code is worse than no gate, so the pure half
now has its own tests: the first commit carries the outcome verbatim, a replayed
session_id awards nothing, and two 10,000-case properties for idempotence and
value preservation.

Mutation score for packages/core: 69.57 -> 75.36 overall, ceremony 0.00 -> 100.00.
civil.ts stays at 69.23 until P1 lands the full zone rule.
